ios.desc:
A companion app for Coca's macOS version, in order to check in on your Mac that is kept awake with Coca at any time. Check device battery, thermals, charging state, deep control, lapsed time and more from your iPhone, while your Mac is working. All using local connectivity, absolute private and no third party involved. Get notified if your MacBook is running out of battery or whether it went to sleep while your work was running!

Coca is commonly used to override macOS energy saving settings and keep your Mac running during presentations, long downloads, backups and many more such scenarios. A brand new addition to such workflows is the use of AI agents with a closed MacBook. Coca on macOS can allow your MacBook to keep running while it has the lid closed, no power cable or external monitor needed. Just one checkbox in Coca settings and it keeps running with closed lid. Together with the iOS app a perfect combination to stay in control of your setup with maximum flexibility.

Key Features

• Prevent your system from sleeping
• Stop the display from dimming or starting screen savers
• Quickly enable or disable from the menu bar
• Optional timers to automatically turn Coca off
• Focus Filters and Shortcuts support
• Closed Lid Mode for laptops

quotes.text:
Not sure how "mostly unknown" these are, but I use:

Work (Macbook):

- Coca: Keeps the screen on and bypasses the "screen lock after X minutes" thing that IT had set up. It's a quality of life adjustment when I'm trying to read something without the screen locking up after a minute. https://apps.apple.com/us/app/coca/id1000808993?mt=12

- Rectangle: Lets me move and resize windows using keyboard shortcuts or snap areas. https://rectangleapp.com/

Browser:

- Weava: Lets me highlight webpages and keep copies of them in a repository for future review. I've been reading a lot of docs lately and it's been a lifesaver. https://www.weavatools.com/

- Bypass Paywalls: Self-explanatory. Also available for FF. https://github.com/iamadamdev/bypass-paywalls-chrome

- Stylus: Can write custom CSS for webpages. You can use other people's styles, but I prefer writing my own in order to have greater control. Another quality of life adjustment when I don't want to stare at stark white documentation. Also available for FF. https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/stylus/clngdbkpkpeebahjckkjfobafhncgmne?hl=en
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are your favorite apps that are mostly unknown?
